_what: Every unverified-output residue finding present in the outgoing documents on the day lint_submission_residue.py was written (2026-08-28, AUT-PROP-032). Anything NOT in this list fails the build the moment it is written.
_why_a_baseline_and_not_a_wall: The lint_citations precedent, for the same reason: failing the build on findings that already exist produces a red gate the next session switches off, which is worse than no gate. THE BASELINE IS THE FINDING — it names, for the first time, exactly which outgoing document carries which unfilled slot. The count is meant to FALL.
⛔_this_is_not_an_amnesty: A row here says a human read the string and decided it may stand FOR NOW. It does not say the document is ready to send. Nine of these fifteen are the SAME slot — a submission date the repository cannot supply and must not invent — and every one of them still has to be filled or cut before its letter goes to an editor.
⭐_two_rows_are_fixable_today_and_are_rec: nr4a3-fusion-transcriptional-output-cover-letter.md's [ORCID] is a fact this repository already holds (CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json), and nr4a3-fusion-transcriptional-output-SI.md's [] is an empty cell in a column every other row fills. Neither was changed by the cycle that wrote this gate, because a gate's author editing the documents it grades is the shape amendment_guard.py exists to catch; both are reported to the owner instead.
_key: file|rule|matched text — never a line number. A baseline keyed to a line is amnesty for whatever drifts onto that line.

entries.line_when_written: 34 and 78 — ONE ROW COVERS BOTH, because the key is the matched text and not a line
entries.why: Two occurrences of the same string in one file. Line 78 is the LIVE slot (`**Date:** [DATE]`): the submission date, not knowable at commit time and one the repository must not invent. Line 34 is the letter's own ⛔ instruction to whoever sends it, naming the brackets that must be filled or cut first — quoted inside that instruction rather than standing as a slot, and deleting it would remove the only place the requirement is written down.

Quoted inside the note recording that this bracket was REMOVED from the letter, because no preprint exists and a bracket in a letter where no preprint exists is 'a sentence waiting to become false'. The removal is the finding; the quotation records it.

Quoted inside a superseded-retained note stating that no [ARCHIVE DOI] placeholder survives — the DOI was minted 2026-08-20. The live placeholder this string names is gone; the record of it is required by CLAUDE.md rule 1.2.
The live `**Date:** [DATE]` slot. The send date is not knowable at commit time; it is filled by the sender, and this gate exists so that it is filled rather than shipped.

⚠ A REAL HOLE, NOT A CONVENTION. The NDRG2 row's driver column is `[]` where every other row of that table names one (`NR4A3 (native)`, `EWSR1::NR4A3`). It renders as a literal `[]` in the built SI. If the intended meaning is 'no driver established for this class-D association', the cell must say so; if a value was dropped, it must be restored. Left as a finding for the document's owner rather than guessed at by the gate's author.
